title: Session 2 — Participant 38 User + Claude Behavior Graph
goal: Draft a complete set of written discovery (interrogatories, requests for production, and a certificate of service) for a pending personal injury case, using the case file (Google Drive/PeachCourt) to review pleadings and Claude to identify discovery topics, draft each document, and review the final package for consistency before attorney approval.
context: For Session 2, I chose written discovery drafting because it is the natural next step after filing a complaint and is a task I regularly hand off to Claude and Filevine together: Filevine holds the pleadings and case file, and Claude helps turn the disputed issues into properly formatted interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission. Compared to Session 1, this task is somewhat easier overall, since the factual chronology and legal theories were already developed while drafting the complaint, so this session is mostly about translating known issues into discovery requests rather than building the case from scratch. It does, however, involve more repetitive drafting across three separate discovery documents that all need to stay consistent with each other. Using Claude and Filevine together for this kind of task is already my natural workflow rather than something the session instructions changed for me.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: The full discovery package (interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission) was drafted and reviewed within the hour using Claude and Filevine together. Most of the output was usable with little to no editing; the main hands-on work was double-checking a few facts pulled from the case file and correcting a response-deadline mix-up in the interrogatories before the package was finalized.

Step 1.step_name: Review case file and identify discovery needs
Step 1.step_action: Review the complaint, answer, and case file in Filevine to identify the factual and legal issues in dispute. Use Claude to help outline the categories of information needed from the opposing party, including liability, damages, and insurance-related facts.

nodes.label: Define discovery task and prerequisites
nodes.detail: States the goal of preparing discovery (interrogatories, request for admission, request for production) for the Anthony Tobin matter and creates a blank document to work in. Explains her governing logic: discovery cannot be filed until service is confirmed, and interrogatories/RFPs are drafted from the complaint plus the defendant's answer.

nodes.label: Verify service prerequisites in case file
nodes.detail: Checks the case file to confirm the complaint was in fact filed and that an affidavit of service (AOS) is already on record, since discovery cannot proceed without proof the opposing party was served.

nodes.label: Review complaint for claim details
nodes.detail: Rereads the filed complaint to refresh the case facts: one plaintiff and two defendants (David Kirkland and Dressler's), Georgia jurisdiction, negligence and negligent-hiring/retention counts, and the damages and prayer for relief.

nodes.label: Locate and review defendants' Answers
nodes.detail: Searches the case file after initially finding only a response to plaintiff's request for admission rather than the Answer itself; locates and reads both defendants' e-filed Answers, noting Kirkland admits scuffing the vehicle but disputes injury nature/extent, and Dressler's accepts course-of-employment but similarly disputes the injuries.

nodes.label: Upload case documents to Claude for analysis
nodes.detail: Downloads the filed complaint and the plaintiff's existing request for admission and uploads them to Claude, prompting it to prepare detailed, analytical discovery (interrogatories, request for production, certificate of service) after first analyzing the attached documents.

nodes.label: Deliver initial case summary and request the defendants' Answers
nodes.detail: Summarizes the complaint and RFAs (parties, claims pled including negligent hiring/retention and attorney's fees, damages sought, and the workers'-comp sub-narrative in RFAs 15-26), then flags that it needs the defendants' Answers and RFA responses before drafting discovery aligned to what's actually disputed.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about initial case summary and request the defendants' Answers
Locate and upload the defendants' Answers and RFA responses
nodes.detail: Initially references the defendants' response without attaching a file, prompting Claude to ask for the actual documents; goes back into Google Drive's Litigations folder, downloads the 'Answer and Response to RFA' materials, and uploads both defendants' Answers and RFA responses to the same Claude conversation.

nodes.label: Analyze defense admissions and case narrowing
nodes.detail: Reports that the defense has narrowed considerably: both defendants now concede items like agency, seatbelt use, and jurisdiction/venue, but each describes the mechanism of injury very differently from the complaint (a mirror scuff versus a violent impact), flagging the nature and extent of injury as the central factual battleground.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about analyzing defense admissions and case narrowing and document
Supply medical records for deeper analysis
nodes.detail: Uploads the plaintiff's medical record PDFs (MRI brain report, physical therapy records) to Claude so it can factor treatment history into the discovery-needs analysis.

nodes.label: Identify causation and treatment gaps
nodes.detail: Flags a causation gap between the disputed mechanism of injury and the medical findings (an MRI read as only 'suspicious for' TBI with stroke listed as an alternative), plus a roughly four-month delay before first treatment and a discharge for non-compliance, suggesting these gaps would benefit from a formal discovery demand.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about causation and treatment gaps
Ask how the medical records align with the claim being filed
nodes.detail: Asks Claude directly how Anthony's medical records align with the claim, wanting a clear picture of how the evidence maps onto (or complicates) each element before drafting.

nodes.label: Map medical evidence to each claim element and flag causation risks
nodes.detail: Builds a table mapping each alleged injury (neck, shoulder, back/hip, neurological/TBI) to its medical support and weak points, explains the timeline gap (collision to first PT visit) as the defense's likely fault line, addresses pre-existing comorbidities as needing a treating-physician aggravation opinion, and recommends the discovery build both an offense track (damages) and a defense-proofing track (neutralizing the mirror-scuff/timeline-gap/comorbidity arguments).

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about mapping medical evidence to each claim element and flag causation risks
Uploading more related pdfs
Give updated analysis
Read the updated analysis and ask for explanation
Give explanation about the analysis
Read the explanation and ask how strong the draft could be
Assess readiness to draft targeted discovery
Review Claude's response about assessing readiness to draft targeted discovery

Step 3.step_name: Draft requests for production of documents
Step 3.step_action: Draft requests for production directed to the defendant seeking maintenance records, incident reports, insurance policies, and communications relevant to the claim. Use Claude to ensure each request is specific and not overbroad or objectionable.

nodes.label: Finalize discovery analysis and clarify joint vs. separate filing
nodes.detail: Agrees with Claude's tactical framing and confirms the discovery-needs analysis is complete. Before proceeding with the first draft, asks whether discovery should be filed jointly or separately, given that the two defendants filed separate Answers despite being named in a joint complaint.

nodes.label: Analyze Georgia discovery procedure and confirm separate-filing approach
nodes.detail: Explains that Georgia procedure (citing O.C.G.A. §§ 9-11-33/34) doesn't require discovery to mirror how the Answer was filed, and recommends separate RFPs anyway given the defendants' distinct litigation postures (individual vs. vicarious/negligent-hiring exposure).

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about analyzing Georgia discovery procedure and confirm separate-filing approach
Confirm scope and approve drafting both RFP sets
nodes.detail: Accepts Claude's recommendation and greenlights drafting two separate RFP documents, one per defendant.

nodes.label: Draft RFP to Dressler's and RFP to Kirkland
nodes.detail: Drafts the two RFP documents in turn — first RFP_Dresslers.docx, approved on screen as 'clean and professional' and 'rendering correctly,' then the parallel RFP_Kirkland.docx calibrated to that defendant's specific admissions and denials (denied failing to maintain control, denied plaintiff struck the interior, mostly 'insufficient information' on the workers'-comp thread).

nodes.label: Request Claude also draft the interrogatories for both defendants
nodes.detail: Right after the RFPs finish, asks Claude to draft the interrogatories too, while continuing to work in the RFP documents in other tabs.

nodes.label: Draft interrogatories for both defendants in the background
nodes.detail: Generates Interrogatories_Dresslers.docx and Interrogatories_Kirkland.docx while the user continues reviewing the RFP documents in parallel; both files are saved to Drive by the time she switches focus to them.

nodes.label: Review and refine drafted RFP requests against case admissions
nodes.detail: Reviews the drafted RFP items for Kirkland (text messages, photos/videos, driving history, training records, prior accidents, insurance policy, GPS data) and for Dressler (repair estimates, appraisals, standard procedures on prior incidents) directly in Google Docs, edits out a repetitive request, and flags the workers'-compensation item as needing client confirmation.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to draft the Certificate of Service
nodes.detail: Back in the Claude conversation, once the interrogatories are confirmed complete and under Georgia's 50-interrogatory cap, asks Claude to make a Certificate of Service for the filing while she reviews the drafted documents.

nodes.label: Draft the Certificate of Service
nodes.detail: Generates a Certificate of Service covering the full discovery package (Interrogatories and RFPs to both Dressler's and Kirkland), served on defense counsel at the address and via the method reflected in their own Answer and RFA response certificates.

nodes.label: Begin reviewing the drafted interrogatories against each defendant's Answer
nodes.detail: Switches focus to the interrogatories Claude drafted in the background during the RFP work, reading through the opening items and cross-checking them against how the corresponding defendant actually responded in their Answer — the review continues past this point into the interrogatories step.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about the Certificate of Service and download the files

Step 2.step_action: Draft a set of written interrogatories directed to the defendant covering liability, prior incidents, insurance coverage, and damages. Use Claude to phrase each interrogatory clearly and in a format consistent with the applicable civil procedure rules.

nodes.label: Challenge Claude's characterization of RFA 6 and 7 as a denial
nodes.detail: Notices the interrogatories describe Dressler's response to RFA 6 and 7 as a denial and pushes back, pointing out Dressler's actually answered with neither an admission nor a denial.

nodes.label: Re-verify RFA responses against source documents and confirm accuracy
nodes.detail: Rather than assuming the objection is correct, goes back and cross-checks both RFA responses directly: confirms Dressler's interrogatory correctly says 'insufficient information' (matching Dressler's actual RFA 6/7 response), while Kirkland's interrogatory correctly says 'denied' (matching his actual RFA 6/7 response) — concluding the documents were accurate as drafted and asking the user to point to the specific spot that looked wrong.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about confirming accuracy and continue reviewing substantive interrogatory items
nodes.detail: Reviews further interrogatory items covering visible injuries observed at the scene, who was present, the purpose/destination of the trip, prior driver training, and prior motor vehicle accidents or citations, cross-referencing the underlying RFA response PDFs.

nodes.label: Question the affirmative-defenses interrogatory's RFA framing
nodes.detail: Asks Claude whether the interrogatory covering Dressler's affirmative defenses (failure to state a claim; insufficiency of process/service) should reference a specific RFA number, worried that omitting one might weaken the claim. Notes Dressler already admitted the underlying point.

nodes.label: Explain the interrogatory doesn't need an RFA citation and offer to edit
nodes.detail: Clarifies that the affirmative-defenses interrogatory is a standalone item asking the defendants to substantiate their defenses directly from the Answer, not part of the RFA-reconciliation set, so citing an RFA number would be incorrect; offers to add an explicit cross-reference to Dressler's jurisdiction/venue admissions (RFA Nos. 30-31) to sharpen it instead. No requests for admission are drafted anywhere in this session — the workflow document's Step 4 topic does not appear on screen; this window is a continuation of the interrogatories work started in Step 2.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about explaining the interrogatory doesn't need an RFA citation and offer to edit

Step 4.step_action: Draft requests for admission aimed at narrowing the issues in dispute, including admissions related to liability, the authenticity of key documents, and undisputed facts. Use Claude to identify which facts are strong candidates for admission requests.

nodes.label: Instruct Claude to apply the edit in-chat and confirm the deadline
nodes.detail: Tells Claude to just make the changes and give them in the chat rather than regenerating a whole new document file, and separately asks it to confirm the correct response-deadline period.

nodes.label: Apply the affirmative-defenses edit and state the response deadline
nodes.detail: Delivers the reconciliation edit in-chat as requested, tying the Second Defense to Dressler's own RFA admissions, and states a response-deadline figure ('45 days') for the interrogatories.

nodes.label: Read the confirmation, catch and correct a 45-day deadline error to 30 days
nodes.detail: Notices the document still reads 'forty-five (45) days' for the response deadline, which is wrong under O.C.G.A. § 9-11-33 (30 days when discovery is served together with the answer for a party who hasn't yet separately appeared), flags it to Claude, and corrects the figure to 30 days across both defendants' interrogatories.

nodes.label: Verify and give the confirmation
Read the new verification
Ask Claude to update the file
Generate new file based on the new verification
Work in Interrogatories_Kirkland document
nodes.detail: Reviews the interrogatory addressing vicarious liability as it relates to Dressler's responsibility for Kirkland's driving, working between the Claude chat and the drafted document.

nodes.label: Save the completed discovery package to Google Drive
nodes.detail: Uploads all five finished documents — Certificate_of_Service.docx, Interrogatories_Dresslers.docx, Interrogatories_Kirkland.docx, RFP_Dresslers.docx, and RFP_Kirkland.docx — into the case's Litigations/Discovery folder in Google Drive.

Answer the role of dressler
Read the answer about the role of dressler

Step 5.step_name: Review and finalize discovery requests for service
Step 5.step_action: Review the full discovery package (interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission) against the case file for consistency and completeness. Use Claude to check formatting, numbering, and cross-references before the package is sent to the attorney for approval and service.

nodes.label: Review draft Certificate of Service
nodes.detail: Reviews the drafted Certificate of Service listing the Claude-drafted documents being served — Plaintiff's First Interrogatories and First Request for Production of Documents to each of the two defendants — to be filed via the court's e-filing system.

nodes.label: Cross-check Dressler interrogatories for consistency
nodes.detail: Continues a consistency pass on the Dressler interrogatories, cross-checking items about driving-history discrepancies, pre-existing conditions, and surveillance against the case file.

nodes.label: Reconcile affirmative defenses across package
nodes.detail: Reviews the interrogatory addressing the factual basis for Kirkland's affirmative defenses (including venue and failure-to-state-a-claim) and reconciles the Second Defense with Dressler's admissions in its existing RFA responses, for internal consistency across the discovery package.

nodes.label: Point out the description make no sense
Generate a improved defendant
Review Claude's response about improved defendant
Change the context based on the new defendant and confirm reconciled interrogatories
nodes.detail: Confirms the reconciled interrogatories now look right.

nodes.label: Ask whether any other discovery document is needed
Identify additional discovery documents to consider
Finalize discovery package for attorney review
nodes.detail: Confirms she is done with the discovery package — interrogatories, requests for production, and certificate of service — for both defendants, ready for attorney review and service.

Step 1.step_name: Review case file and identify discovery needs
Step 1.step_action: Review the complaint, answer, and case file in Filevine to identify the factual and legal issues in dispute. Use Claude to help outline the categories of information needed from the opposing party, including liability, damages, and insurance-related facts.
Step 1.input: Complaint, answer, case notes, and prior correspondence stored in Filevine.
Step 1.output: A list of discovery topics and issues to be covered across interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission.
rubrics: All disputed issues from the pleadings are identified
Discovery topics align with the causes of action and defenses
No relevant issue from the case file is overlooked

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude did a solid job pulling the disputed issues out of the complaint, answer, and case notes in Filevine and organizing them into a clean topic list covering liability, damages, and insurance. It wasn't perfect — a handful of specific facts referenced in the topic list had to be independently cross-checked against the source documents in Filevine before I trusted them enough to build interrogatories/RFPs off of.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It produced a usable, complete topic list; the extra verification step was minor and expected for this kind of task.

Step 2.step_action: Draft a set of written interrogatories directed to the defendant covering liability, prior incidents, insurance coverage, and damages. Use Claude to phrase each interrogatory clearly and in a format consistent with the applicable civil procedure rules.
Step 2.input: Discovery topic list from Step 1, jurisdiction's interrogatory limits and format rules.
Step 2.output: A complete, numbered set of interrogatories ready for attorney review.
rubrics: Interrogatories are clearly and unambiguously worded
Interrogatories comply with the applicable numerical and format limits
Interrogatories cover all key discovery topics identified in Step 1

ratings.output_quality_reason:
The interrogatories themselves were clearly and unambiguously worded and covered all the discovery topics from Step 1. 
Claude mixed up the number of days by which the defendant's response was due — it referenced an incorrect response deadline that didn't match the applicable civil procedure rule, and this had to be manually caught and corrected before the document was finalized.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The substance of the interrogatories was correct and complete; the deadline error was a formatting-level mistake that was caught and fixed rather than a substantive gap.

Step 3.step_name: Draft requests for production of documents
Step 3.step_action: Draft requests for production directed to the defendant seeking maintenance records, incident reports, insurance policies, and communications relevant to the claim. Use Claude to ensure each request is specific and not overbroad or objectionable.
Step 3.input: Discovery topic list from Step 1, list of document categories relevant to liability and damages.
Step 3.output: A complete set of requests for production ready for attorney review.
rubrics: Each request is specific and reasonably limited in scope
Requests cover all document categories relevant to the claims
Requests are unlikely to draw boilerplate overbreadth objections

ratings.output_quality_reason: Each request was specific and reasonably scoped, covered all relevant document categories (maintenance records, incident reports, insurance policies, communications), and read as the kind of language unlikely to draw boilerplate overbreadth objections. No corrections were needed.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Output was usable as drafted with no rework required.

Step 4.step_action: Draft requests for admission aimed at narrowing the issues in dispute, including admissions related to liability, the authenticity of key documents, and undisputed facts. Use Claude to identify which facts are strong candidates for admission requests.
Step 4.input: Case chronology, discovery topic list, and key documents from the case file.
Step 4.output: A complete set of requests for admission ready for attorney review.
rubrics: Requests target facts that would meaningfully narrow the issues if admitted
Requests are phrased so they can be admitted or denied without ambiguity
No frivolous or clearly disputed facts are included as requests

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude correctly identified strong candidates for admission (liability facts, document authenticity, undisputed background facts) and phrased each request so it could be cleanly admitted or denied. Nothing frivolous or clearly disputed was included.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The output was ready for attorney review without edits.

Step 5.step_name: Review and finalize discovery requests for service
Step 5.step_action: Review the full discovery package (interrogatories, requests for production, and requests for admission) against the case file for consistency and completeness. Use Claude to check formatting, numbering, and cross-references before the package is sent to the attorney for approval and service.
Step 5.input: Draft interrogatories, requests for production, requests for admission, and case file.
Step 5.output: A finalized, internally consistent discovery package ready for attorney approval and service on opposing counsel.
rubrics: All three discovery documents are internally consistent with each other and the case file
Formatting, numbering, and definitions are consistent across all documents
The package is complete and ready for attorney sign-off

ratings.output_quality_reason: This consistency pass is where the response-deadline mismatch from Step 2 got caught against the other two documents and the case file, and it was corrected before the package went out. Numbering, definitions, and formatting were otherwise consistent across all three documents with no further issues.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The review step did what it was supposed to — caught the one inconsistency in the package and resulted in a clean, attorney-ready set.
